newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion closing arguments delayed.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion closing arguments delayed.

text.p: U.S. District Court Judge Carlton Tilley delayed closing arguments in the punitive damages phase of Food Lion Inc's lawsuit against Walt Disney Co's ABC Television while lawyers finalized the wording of proposed instructions to the jury.

The judge said the arguments would begin at 1330 EST/1830 GMT on Monday, giving lawyers in the case time to work out the proposed jury instructions. Following the arguments, the instructions will be given to the jury by the judge, and the panel will decide how much, if anything, Food Lion ought to receive in punitive damages.

Food Lion is suing ABC for its hidden-camera report that charged the Salisbury, North Carolina-based grocery chain sold spoiled meat and out-dated produce, and used unsanitary food handling practices. The program aired on ABC's "PrimeTime Live" program in 1992.
Food Lion was reported to be seeking punitive damages of nearly $2 billion dollars but representatives from the grocer have declined comment.
The federal jury hearing the case last month found ABC was liable for fraud.
The panel awarded the grocer $1,400 in actual damages, but could award a much higher amount in punitive damages if it found that ABC willfully broke the law and profited from its actions.
On Friday, ABC wrapped up evidence in the punishment phase of the trial with testimony from Dianne Sawyer, star co-anchor of the PrimeTime Live show.
